steps.title: Malbec
steps.body: Malbec is Mendoza's signature, with about 70% of Argentina's Malbec. It gives deep purple wines with plum, blackberry, violet and cocoa, and soft, ripe tannins. It arrived in 1853 with French agronomist Michel Aimé Pouget, hired to found an agricultural school. April 17, the date of the school's founding law, is now World Malbec Day.

steps.title: Others
steps.body: Bonarda, the same as Douce Noir from Savoie, not Italy's Bonarda, is Argentina's second most planted red, giving fruity, soft wines. Cabernet Sauvignon is important, often blended with Malbec. Cabernet Franc has become a rising star. Whites include Chardonnay, Torrontés and Sémillon. Criolla Grande and Cereza, pink-skinned, make bulk wine.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.

steps.body: Argentine Bonarda is not the same as Italian Bonarda. DNA shows it's Douce Noir, from France's Savoie.

steps.explanation: Marking the 1853 founding of Mendoza's agricultural school.
